title: Jesus Probably Wasn't Born on 25 December
desc: Even Japan, with very few Christians, goes all in on Christmas. But the date itself? Probably not his birthday.

title: The Bible Never Gives Jesus's Birthday
desc: Luke and Matthew tell the story, but never the date. One early guess put it on 20 May.

title: Why Christmas Is on 25 December
desc: The first recorded Christmas was in Rome in 336, right next to the feast of the Unconquered Sun.

title: Christmas Traditions That Are Older Than Christmas
desc: Mistletoe from the Celts, Yule logs from the Norse, gifts from Roman Saturnalia.

title: The Vatican Had No Christmas Tree Until 1982
desc: Carols began as Koleda, the tree began in medieval Livonia, and the Vatican held out for centuries.

title: What Christmas Colours Really Mean
desc: Red, green and gold all have a meaning. Or, if you ask the shops, red is for Santa.

title: Santa Was a Real Man from Turkey
desc: Saint Nicholas of Myra gave away his fortune and became the protector of children.

title: How Sinterklaas Became Santa Claus
desc: Dutch families brought him to New York. Say Sinterklaas fast enough and you get Santa Claus.

title: Santa Used to Wear Green
desc: Early Santas wore green, blue or white. 1930s Coca-Cola adverts made the red suit famous worldwide.

title: Not Every Country Gets Santa
desc: An angel child in Germany, an elf with goats in Sweden, a Yule Goat in Finland, a witch in Italy.

title: Why Spanish Kids Open Presents on 6 January
desc: For centuries Epiphany was the bigger day. In Spain the Day of the Kings still is.

title: A King's Christmas Feast: 28 Oxen and 300 Sheep
desc: Charlemagne and William the Conqueror were crowned on Christmas Day. Richard II threw the biggest party.

title: When Christmas Was Banned
desc: Gifts once went from tenants to landlords on 6 January. Then the Puritans banned Christmas altogether. It didn't last.

title: How a Queen Made the Christmas Tree Famous
desc: German-born Queen Charlotte brought the tree to the British court. One picture in 1848 put one in every home.

title: The Whole History of Christmas in One Breath
desc: A birthday on a borrowed date, a tree from Livonia, a log from the Norse and a saint from Turkey. Happy Christmas!
